claims.text: A post-solution-treatment aging treatment can promote gamma-prime precipitation in a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy.
The precipitated gamma-prime phase will be coherent Ni3Al.
Aging-induced gamma-prime precipitation will enhance elevated-temperature yield strength relative to the unaged alloy.
The starting material can be a homogenized, single-phase titanium- and nickel-primary HEA produced by arc melting and solution treatment.
The proposed alloy contains titanium and nickel as nearly equiatomic primary constituents together with at least three other elements.
An alloy with at least five elements, each at 5–35 at%, satisfies the stated HEA compositional definition.
Adding approximately 5–15 at% aluminum will enable gamma-prime precipitation in the proposed Ti-Ni-primary alloy.
Aging at approximately 800°C for four hours in an inert or vacuum atmosphere will induce nanoscale gamma-prime particles.
The aging treatment will produce a homogeneous dispersion of coherent nanoscale gamma-prime precipitates within the matrix.
Gamma-prime precipitates impede dislocation motion at elevated temperatures.
Impeded dislocation motion caused by gamma-prime precipitates will enhance yield strength and creep resistance.
Aging is predicted to increase elevated-temperature yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to the solution-treated alloy.
Aging is predicted to improve creep resistance relative to the solution-treated alloy.
The proposed strengthening effect is applicable over an operating-temperature range of approximately 800–1200°C.
An aluminum content of 5–15 at% can promote gamma-prime formation without compromising the alloy's multi-principal-element balance.
The magnitude of strengthening and precipitate stability at very high temperatures depends on alloy composition and aging parameters.

The intervention is falsified if aging produces less than a 10% improvement in elevated-temperature yield strength or creep resistance, or if the intended nanoscale gamma-prime precipitates are absent.
